output.review_comment: The off-by-one fix (`top - first + 1`) and the negative-quantity check are correct and match the docstring. But the new open-ended tier logic (`if last is None: total = quantity * price; break`) contradicts the docstring. It throws away the charges from the lower tiers and bills every unit at the bulk rate. That's volume pricing, but the function is `graduated_price_cents` and the docstring (which the teammate called the source of truth) describes graduated tiers. It also makes the price drop at the tier boundary, so 500 units can cost more than 501, which graduated pricing never does. The PR says this came from "analyzing the tests," so it looks like the agent fit the code to a test instead of the spec. Fix: treat the open-ended tier like the others, `top = quantity if last is None else min(quantity, last); total += (top - first + 1) * price`. If a test still fails after that, look into why and raise it with the team instead of changing the pricing model.
